sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas converted to x^0 = c t
sources.locator: Section 1.3.2 pp. 22-23 (light-rectangles); Chapter 2 Sections 2.1.1-2.1.3 pp. 43-45 (arrow of time, initial-value causality, the modest causality postulate P1); Section 4.7 pp. 110-113 (FTL defense in depth, tachyon searches, tachyons and quantum mechanics); printed page numbers as in the PDF text layer

contents.name: Section 1.3.2 pp. 22-23: light-rectangles as the set of events in the 1+1-dimensional plane between two events with edges of slope +-1, and the invariance of the area of the rectangle
contents.support: Recast as the causal diamond J^+(p) intersect J^-(q) computed from the coordinate criterion, with the area invariance checked by det B(b) = 1 for a passive boost; the source's c = 1 reading is not used as a definition.

contents.name: Sections 2.1.1-2.1.2 pp. 43-44: the arrow of time and Laplace-style initial-value causality; the paper literature (Norton; Echeverria et al.) that a general causality principle is not established by the laws of physics
contents.support: The postulate's status clause adopts the causal signal restriction as a model assumption and states explicitly that no general causality principle is derived; the source's skepticism about a grand causality principle is recorded in the postulate's scope rather than converted into a theorem.

contents.name: Section 2.1.3 p. 44: the modest causality postulate P1 (there exist events whose displacement is timelike in all frames) and the reading that cause and effect can be described only for such pairs
contents.support: The source's P1 is an existence postulate about timelike displacements; this page's restriction is a different statement (no signal between spacelike-related events). The source is cited for the reading and the difference is recorded in the batch notes; P1 itself is not re-minted.

contents.name: Section 4.7.1 pp. 110-111: superluminal transmission of information would violate causality because it would allow a causal relationship between spacelike-related events whose time ordering differs between observers; the interpretation of the metric as a statement of possible cause and effect
contents.support: The source’s heuristic argument is realized as the model theorem: clause (v) excludes signals on spacelike-related pairs and clause (i) makes the temporal order of a transmission’s endpoints invariant; the mathematical reason is supplied locally by lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order.

contents.name: Section 4.7.1 pp. 111-112: the tachyonic antitelephone attributed to Tolman and the possibility of messages from the future; the caveat that FTL observers are kinematically impossible in 3+1 dimensions
contents.support: Realized as the conditional relay computation with exact arrival time L(2u - v - vu^2/c^2)/(u - v)^2, with the availability assumptions (fixed speed in each emitter's rest frame, immediate relaying, inertial motion) stated explicitly; the FTL-observer caveat is not used.

contents.name: Section 4.7.2 pp. 112-113: experiments to search for tachyons (cosmic-ray air showers; beta-decay momentum and energy measurement; missing-energy reactions) and their reported negative results
contents.reason: Reported searches are secondary summaries in this textbook; an experiment item requires the primary reports with apparatus, calibration, sampling and uncertainty, which this page does not read and does not fabricate. The design of sr-experimental-interface reserves quantitative empirical interface work.

contents.name: Section 4.7.3 p. 113: tachyons and quantum mechanics; speculative remarks on reinterpretation and spin-statistics
contents.reason: Quantum postulates are outside the flat classical special-relativity framework of this page; no quantum framework, quantum-field or spin-statistics assumption is available here, and the item would need its own framework.

sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997); PDF page = printed page + 7
sources.locator: Chapter 1 pp. 5-7 (light cones and separation); Chapter 4 pp. 124-127 (causality, domains of dependence, Misner space); printed page numbers as in the arXiv PDF

contents.name: Chapter 1 pp. 6-7: light cones are invariant under Lorentz transformations, split into future and past; timelike, spacelike and null separated points, and the impossibility of a coordinate-independent future/past position for a spacelike-separated point
contents.support: Made exact: part (a) records the pure spatial inequality in every inertial chart; parts (b)-(d) exhibit explicit inertial frames of simultaneity and of either time order through passive boosts, which is the quantitative content of the source’s impossibility statement.

contents.name: Chapter 4 p. 125: the guiding principle that no signals travel faster than the speed of light, so information flows only along timelike or null trajectories
contents.support: The source’s guiding principle is adopted as clause (i) of the causal signal restriction, with its status recorded as an adopted scope assumption rather than a derived or empirical claim.

contents.name: Chapter 4 pp. 125-126: future and past domains of dependence D^+(S), D^-(S), Cauchy horizons, and the insufficiency of a badly chosen initial surface in Minkowski space
contents.reason: Global and curved domains of dependence and field-theoretic finite propagation concern PDE initial-value problems on manifolds; this page proves only the kinematic flat cone statement and explicitly supplies no PDE finite-propagation theorem. The wave page and the EM development own the PDE version.

contents.name: Chapter 4 pp. 126-127: Misner space with closed timelike curves and the failure of a well-defined initial-value problem there
contents.reason: Misner space is not the affine Minkowski model; the affine model has no closed future causal curves (proved locally), and quotient or non-flat spacetimes with closed timelike curves require a different spacetime structure and are not part of this framework.

sources.title: R. C. Tolman, The Theory of the Relativity of Motion (University of California Press, Berkeley, 1917); Internet Archive full text of the 1917 printing; original notation retains c and the (+---)-style transform equations (11)-(12)
sources.locator: Chapter V, Sections 45-47 and 51-52, printed pp. 49-55 (clock rate, simultaneity, velocities greater than light); printed page numbers as in the archive text

contents.name: Sections 45-46 pp. 49-51: the kinematical rate of a moving clock and the proposed canal-ray spectroscopic test
contents.reason: Clock-rate comparisons and the moving-clock analysis are the declared subject of the proper-time-comparisons page; this page uses neither the rate formula nor the proposed observational test, and no measurement is authored.

contents.name: Section 47 p. 51: the idea of absolute simultaneity must be given up; two events simultaneous in one system are not simultaneous in a system moving relative to it (transform equations (11)-(12))
contents.support: The source’s one-way simultaneity shift is made exact as the explicit family x_b of inertial charts, including the frame of simultaneity and the frames of either time order for a spacelike-separated pair.

contents.name: Section 51 pp. 53-54: composition of velocities never produces a speed exceeding that of light when the composed velocities do not exceed it
contents.reason: Velocity composition is the subject of the Lorentz-transformations page, where it is proved for the model's boosts; this page does not restate it and only uses the boost matrix for spacelike displacements, so the result is neither needed nor re-derived here.

contents.name: Section 52 pp. 54-55: an impulse that is causal from A to B with velocity u greater than that of light yields, in a system moving with velocity V relative to the first, a negative elapsed time (formula (29)): the effect precedes its cause
contents.support: The one-way order reversal is realized as the sign of the return time difference Delta t under the threshold v > 2u/(1+u^2/c^2) in clause (b) of the relay computation, with the two-way closed chain supplied locally.

contents.name: Section 52 p. 55: the blocks and alarm-clock example: kinematic occurrences without causal connection, and without transfer of energy, need not be slower than light
contents.support: Recomputed as an explicit family of spacelike-separated events with sweep speed w > c, shown to be simultaneous in a boosted frame; the example supports the non-restriction clause of post-sr-causal-signal-propagation.

contents.name: Section 52 p. 55: the conclusion that the extraordinary nature of the order reversal inclines one to believe that no causal impulse travels faster than light
contents.support: Recorded as the motivation of the adopted restriction; the item states explicitly that the source’s inclination is not a proof and that the restriction is an assumption of the model.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Mathematical Tripos Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision); Internet Archive copy of the original https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/hsr1000/part3_gr_lectures.pdf
sources.locator: Sections 2.1-2.3, printed pp. 25-30 (PDF pp. 26-31); printed page = PDF page - 1

contents.name: Section 2.1 p. 25: the Minkowski metric eta = -(dx^0)^2 + (dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2 + (dx^3)^2 and inertial frames as charts with eta_mu nu = diag(-1,1,1,1)
contents.support: The sign convention is already fixed by the run's own def-lorentz-form-and-inertia and def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart; the source is cited for the coordinate criterion computation in that convention.

contents.name: Section 2.2 p. 27: timelike, null, spacelike and causal vectors, the light-cone double cone of an orthonormal basis, and the fact that the causal vectors fall into two disconnected sets
contents.support: The two-components statement is the run's lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components; the source confirms the geometric reading used in the cone description and the coordinate criterion.

contents.name: Section 2.2 pp. 27-28: O(1,3) as the matrices with Lambda^T eta Lambda = eta, and the transformation of vector components between orthonormal bases
contents.support: The boost computation realizes the spacelike-pair time-order family through explicit passive boosts; the source supplies the convention Lambda^T eta Lambda = eta that the run's def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group uses.

contents.name: Section 2.3 pp. 28-30: timelike and causal curves, proper time (2.19), and curves of extremal proper time; in Minkowski space the extremal timelike curves are straight lines and it is stated, without proof, that they maximize proper time
contents.support: The source states the maximization of proper time along straight timelike lines without proof; clause (e) of the theorem supplies the complete proof (boost normalization, pointwise inequality, equality case) for piecewise C^1 future timelike worldlines.

canonical.name: Framework definitions: causal reachability relation, causal and chronological futures and pasts, causal diamonds, and reachability by future causal paths
canonical.support: The page's own definition item, built from the model, the causal classification and the time orientation; no chart or physical premise enters.

canonical.name: Framework lemma: description of the closed future cone in inertial coordinates and the coordinate criterion for causal reachability, with finite-sum closure
canonical.support: Proved from the orthonormal-basis expansion of eta and the triangle inequality; supplies the computational form used by every later item on the page.

canonical.name: Framework theorem: future causal paths have future causal displacements, J^+ and I^+ equal the path-reachable sets, no causal loops exist, inertial coordinate time is monotone, and the straight worldline maximizes proper time
canonical.support: The stable research item thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence placed on this page by the splice, with the flat proper-time maximum proved locally; no PDE finite propagation is supplied.

canonical.name: Framework postulate: the causal signal restriction, with the ideal-light boundary case and the explicit non-restrictions
canonical.support: Adopted assumption, sourced to the three treatments and reviewed as a postulate rather than a theorem or an empirical result.

canonical.name: Framework theorem: receipt in the future cone, absolute temporal order of a transmission's endpoints, relay composition, no closed signal loops, frame independence, exclusion of spacelike signal pairs
canonical.support: Conditional physical reading of the mathematical items, with scope and qualification; no apparatus, measurement or statistical content.

canonical.name: Framework thought experiment: the one-relay superluminal signal chain received in the strict past of its emission
canonical.support: Complete conditional computation with stated availability assumptions; not an empirical observation and not a claim that such devices exist.
